sources.entry: LuxShot - Native and privacy-first menu bar OCR tool. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/lukebuild/LuxShot) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: LuxShot is a native macOS menu bar app for on-device OCR text capture from any screen region, plus QR and barcode scanning.
summary.what_it_does: LuxShot runs in the macOS menu bar and lets you select a region of the screen to recognize its text using Apple's Vision framework (VNRecognizeTextRequest). It also detects and decodes QR codes and barcodes (VNDetectBarcodesRequest). Options include keeping or removing line breaks, auto-opening URLs found in captured text, and auto-copying recognized text to the clipboard. Recognized text can be read aloud with AVSpeechSynthesizer, and a history of recent scans is kept. The README states all processing happens on-device.
use_cases: Copy text from an image or screen region that cannot be selected
Scan QR codes or barcodes on screen
Extract text from a PDF or video frame shown on screen
Keep a local history of recent screen OCR scans
Capture text privately without uploading to a cloud service
how_to_run: Download the latest .zip from the Releases page
Drag LuxShot.app to the Applications folder
Right-click LuxShot.app and choose Open, then confirm (needed because the app is not notarized)
Launch LuxShot and press Cmd + Shift + E, or click New Scan in the menu bar popover
To build from source: clone the repo, open LuxShot.xcodeproj in Xcode, set the signing team (or None), and press Command + R
notable: On-device OCR and barcode detection with no cloud processing, per the README
Menu bar-only workflow with a global shortcut (Cmd + Shift + E)
Built with SwiftUI and AppKit, using Apple's native Vision framework
Optional auto-copy and auto-open of detected links
caveats: Not distributed via the App Store and not notarized, so macOS shows a security warning on first launch
Building from source requires Xcode and a signing team setup or None for local testing
